Abstract: In this review article, we will explore the recent advancements in the field of distributed control of modular multilevel cascaded converters (MMCCs), highlighting the key challenges and opportunities in this area. The article will delve into the various control strategies that have been proposed and evaluate their performance in different scenarios, considering three main aspects: 1) the MMCC voltage and power level, 2) the MMCC topology being considered [e.g., the modular multilevel matrix converter (M3C) and the hexverter], and 3) the application being considered [e.g., drive applications, static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs), etc.]. This review work aims to help researchers by providing an overview of the current state of the art in the field of distributed control of MMCCs. It will point them toward the gaps in current research and provide inspiration for future work. For practicing engineers, the article will provide a detailed understanding of the control strategies and technologies used in MMCCs. It will highlight the key challenges and opportunities in the field, allowing engineers to make informed and cost-effective decisions when designing and implementing MMCCs in practical applications.

Abstract: The device-level description of power switches is an emerging topic that enhances the real-time simulation (RTS) accuracy of power electronic converters. Therefore, much research has sought the tradeoff between the accuracy and speed in DLRTSs. In this article, we review state-of-the-art DLRTS technologies, in particular for device-level switch models and efficient network solvers. Moreover, we summarize different applications of DLRTSs and crosswise compare their performances. We also give some outlooks on future research. This review not only provides a comprehensive overview of DLRTSs for general audiences but also provides a technical reference for practitioners. Abstract: The solid-state transformer (SST) was conceived as a replacement for the conventional power transformer, with both lower volume and weight. Abstract: This lart, 1,108-page book is the second extended edition of the popular book published by Academic Press in 2006. This new edition is inspired by the continuous development of power electronic systems, which—as noted by Prof. Bose—are the basis of the era of the third revolution of the 21st century and of the development of our civilization in general. This is due to the observed encroachment of power electronics, not only in industrial systems but also in such important areas of our lives as renewable and distributed energy (smart grids) and the fight against global warming. Each chapter in the book begins with an abstract and a clear introduction and ends with a constructive conclusion. Moreover, each chapter contains a list of publications and—what should be emphasized—many of them were updated. The book also contains a list of abbreviations, a list of variables and symbols, and an index. Power Electronics and Motor Drives: Advances and Trends is a valuable tool for graduate researchers, practicing engineers, and scientists working in the areas of power electronics and controlled drives as well as renewable and distributed energy systems. It provides the needed technical background for each subject, and therefore it can also be recommended for senior undergraduates and master’s level students of electrical engineering and power system studies interested in modern power electronics energy systems. I strongly believe that this new edition of Prof. Bose’s stateof-the-art book will be as successful as the previous eight books bearing the author's name.
